key_insight: A biologically informed dual‑branch transformer separates intrinsic cell state from drug‑induced regulatory shifts, enabling accurate prediction of transcriptional responses across doses and times. This disentangling lets the model capture nonlinear dose–time dynamics and generalize to unseen cellular contexts.
problem_solved: Predicting how cells' gene expression changes under different drugs, doses and timepoints is hard because intrinsic cell state and perturbation effects are entangled and dynamics are nonlinear; the paper addresses robust, generalizable prediction of these responses.
method: Dual‑branch transformer architecture: one branch models baseline cell state, the other models drug‑induced regulatory shifts, with a learned fusion layer to produce perturbed expression.
Biologically informed priors/constraints: pathway or regulatory structure and dose/time encodings guide the transformer to respect known biology and temporal nonlinearity.

Latent disentanglement and dose–time modeling: separate latent representations for cell vs perturbation, plus mechanisms to capture nonlinear dose‑response and temporal dynamics for prediction and generalization.
impact: Provides a scalable, interpretable deep‑learning recipe for predicting drug perturbations that ML practitioners can adapt for biology‑aware modeling tasks; improves transferability to new cell types and experimental regimes.
visual_elements: Schematic of the dual‑branch transformer showing Cell branch, Drug/Perturbation branch, dose/time encoders, and fusion→predicted expression
Dose–time response surface or heatmap comparing ground truth vs predictions across doses and timepoints
Latent space visualization (e.g., t-SNE/UMAP) demonstrating separation of cell state vs perturbation embeddings
Bar/line charts of generalization performance: seen vs unseen cell types and benchmarks against baselines
paper_title: Modelling drug-induced cellular perturbation responses with a biologically informed dual-branch transformer
paper_authors: Yue Guo, Hao Zhang, Haitao Hu, Jialu Wu, Ji Cao
